title: Apple visionOS glass material
lede: Windows in Apple’s headset are made of a system glass that blurs the real room behind them.
summary: visionOS windows use an adaptive frosted glass over the physical surroundings. Apple, 2023.
made: 2023 (visionOS unveiled June 5, 2023; HIG visionOS guidance added June 21, 2023)

evidence.note: Read the HIG Materials page (through its JSON data and in Claude in Chrome) and inspected its image visionos-materials-window-example@2x.png (1184 × 746) and the Apple Newsroom image Apple-WWDC23-Vision-Pro-VisionOS-230605 (1960 × 1102) in scratchpad copies. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit. The glass, blur, radii, and opacity levels match, but the backdrop is a real room, not vivid color. NN/g and Everyday UX use it as a current example.

context: The HIG says visionOS windows “generally use an unmodifiable system-defined material called glass” that lets light, the current Environment, virtual content, and physical objects show through. Glass adapts to the luminance behind it, so visionOS has no separate Dark Mode. [Apple HIG: Materials](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/materials).

It advises: “Prefer translucency to opaque colors in windows.” The thin material marks interactive elements, regular separates sections such as a sidebar, and thick makes a dark element on top of regular. Vibrancy is applied to text and symbols on the glass.

NN/g writes that the Apple Vision Pro “uses glassmorphic SwiftUI materials in translucent UI overlays”. [NN/g 2024](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/glassmorphism/). Apple says the 2025 [Liquid Glass](ref:apple-liquid-glass-2025) design was “inspired by the depth and dimensionality of visionOS”.
observed: HIG diagram: a large window with rounded corners floats in a beige living room. The room behind it is blurred to soft shapes of furniture and a red object.
The window has a darker sidebar (regular), a dark text-field bar at the top (thick), and a lighter button at the lower right (thin). All are translucent.
Newsroom image: the App Store window floats in a room; a vertical, pill-shaped tab bar at its left edge is translucent and shows the wall behind it.
The window’s content (a star field with a constellation bear) is opaque; the glass appears in the chrome and control areas.
interpretation: visionOS moves the style off the gradient and onto the world: the backdrop becomes the user’s own room. It keeps the three-level opacity hierarchy that web glassmorphism uses.
borrow: Define three glass thicknesses and give each one a job: thin for controls, regular for sections, thick for dark overlays.

rights.statement: Apple documentation and press images; copyrighted. No image is stored here.
